If you and I sat down together, I think we’d walk away as friends...
In fact, I think we’d leave as close allies in a battle for our country's future.
****[This is Vivek Ramaswamy: I’m a husband, a father, and an America First fighter who’s sick and tired of watching our country lose its spine.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MTAwNl9TNy1XUC4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyMDQtMzYyMyZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjEwMDZfUzctV1AuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDQ3MjA0LTM2MjMifQ/9RIpFYUAKZnNKMtLvxPzmA)
Why does the single mom in Toledo have to work two jobs while illegal immigrants get handed luxury hotel rooms, healthcare, and debit cards?
Why are kids in Cincinnati stepping over used needles while bureaucrats lecture them about “inclusion”?
Let’s call this what it is: America is being hollowed out from the inside.
And I’m not here to nibble around the edges.
[I’m running for Governor to overhaul the system from the ground up. I believe Ohio can be the beating heart of America’s revival.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MTAwNl9TNy1XUC4xMTAxMTdfdDIwNDcyMDQtMzYyMyZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjEwMDZfUzctV1AuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDQ3MjA0LTM2MjMifQ/H7cvmPp99lUTgMg1_RLaTg)
That’s why my entire campaign is centered on:
1) Supporting President Trump's America First Agenda.2) Cutting red tape3) Slashing taxes4) Empowering families5) Unleashing innovation
And let me tell you, the Democrat Machine is ENRAGED by this mission. They’ll do everything they can to stop me from winning this race.

# When the Safety System Wasn’t Safe
| |
---
|
---
A September 16 investigation published by [_The BMJ_ ](https://xdzgmz.clicks.mlsend.com/ty/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEyMDEyNjAsXCJsXCI6MjAwNTgwOTYxMDA1NDcxMDkyLFwiclwiOjIwMDU4MDk5OTc1NDU0ODg2OH0iLCJzIjoiMzVlNWEyODczMGE5ODk3YSJ9)confirms what medical-liberty advocates have argued for years: federal health officials did not provide an honest account of what their own vaccine-safety systems could and could not see. “US officials embraced an algorithm for detecting signals of harm from mRNA covid-19 vaccines,” _The BMJ_ reported, “that they knew was broken and suppressed efforts to fix it.” **Here’s how the problem worked:** The algorithm compared one COVID vaccine largely against the other. If Pfizer and Moderna increased the risk of the same adverse event by similar amounts, the rates could look essentially the same. No meaningful difference meant no alert. Statisticians call this _masking, a flaw that can create false reassurance rather than evidence of safety._ This failure was not subtle or discovered years later and quietly corrected. According to the investigation, federal health officials knew about the problem in 2021 and continued using the system while assuring us that these products were **“safe & effective,” language that was also used to justify vaccine mandates.** That raises a fundamental question about informed consent: How can Americans **make truly informed medical decisions** when the government withholds known limitations in the very systems designed to detect potential harms? Whether that failure was negligence or something more deliberate, the result was the same: Americans were given assurances of safety without being given the full picture. **And there has still been no serious reckoning.** TFVC is fighting to make sure Texans never have to surrender that right to a government mandate or a promise of “safe & effective.” **To that end, look for our General Election Voter Guide coming next week!**

If Pfizer and Moderna increased the risk of the same adverse event by similar amounts, the rates could look essentially the same. No meaningful difference meant no alert. Statisticians call this masking, a flaw that can create false reassurance rather than evidence of safety. This failure was not subtle or discovered years later and quietly corrected. That raises a fundamental question about informed consent: How can Americans make truly informed medical decisions when the government withholds known limitations in the very systems designed to detect potential harms? Whether that failure was negligence or something more deliberate, the result was the same: Americans were given assurances of safety without being given the full picture. Nicholas Farrish did exactly what the law tells people in his position to do. After a felony conviction, he served his sentence, finished his supervision, and rebuilt his life. Then he asked a Mississippi court to restore the firearm rights his conviction had stripped away, a path the statute itself lays out.
What happened next should give every Mississippian pause. A circuit judge weighed the evidence and found, in writing, that Farrish is fully rehabilitated and that his possessing a firearm "would not be dangerous to public safety." That is not a hunch or a technicality. It is a judicial finding, made after a hearing.
And then the same judge gave him back only part of what he had asked for. Long guns, yes. A handgun, no. And whatever firearm he does keep must sit locked in a safe whenever it is not in his hands.
Think about what this means. The only justification for disarming a citizen is the threat they pose to public safety. Taking their guns protects the community. But the State concedes there is no danger here. A judge found this man safe, and the State does not dispute it. Once the danger is gone, so is the reason.
Yet the State still claims the power to tell a man, it admits is harmless, which guns he may own, long guns, yes; a pistol, no, and to make him lock the rest in a safe inside his own home. If he is safe, he is safe with a handgun too; the risk is in the person, not the type of gun. This is not public safety. This is the government treating a constitutional right as a privilege, arbitrarily granting it to citizens as it pleases.
Farrish's felony was a third DUI. Drunk driving kills, it shatters families, and Mississippi is right to treat it as a grave offense. But Farrish is not a predator, and the judge who heard every fact of it found he poses a danger to no one.
Most of us have never really thought this through. We hear "convicted felon" and we nod when the government takes the guns away. It feels like plain common sense. But look closer. We are not talking about arming someone a court believes is dangerous. We are talking about a specific man a court found safe and a government that still refuses to fully let go.
This is no longer an abstract debate. Farrish's case is now before the Mississippi Supreme Court, and Attorney General Lynn Fitch's office has just filed the State's brief. I have read all thirty-two pages. Fitch's lawyers argue that a convicted felon, any convicted felon, has no Second Amendment right in the first place. They argue the courts need not even ask whether a particular person is actually dangerous. And they defend the lock-and-key order on a man already found rehabilitated as a perfectly reasonable condition.
Nowhere in those thirty-two pages does Fitch's brief cite the Mississippi Constitution, which guarantees the right of "every citizen" to keep and bear arms.
Here is the uncomfortable truth the case lays bare. A right the government can switch off for an entire class of people and leave off even after a judge rules the danger gone is not really a right at all. It is a privilege, handed back when the state decides it feels like it.
Farrish served his time. A judge said he is safe. The only question left is whether "shall not be infringed" still means something in Mississippi, or whether our rights now come with a combination lock.

Hi, it’s Sherrod again. I'll keep this quick: Early voting starts today in Ohio, and we're behind on our October fundraising goal, so I'm personally reaching out for help.

I don't rely on shady megadonors or super PACs to fuel this campaign, so I'm being genuine when I say this: **I don't have anywhere else to turn. You are my plan A, B, and C. **

Ten years ago this fall, a single promise carried a candidate to the presidency: "I will build a great wall." Of all the stories born in 2016 -- the hacks, the leaks, the recounts -- none has a longer construction record, a bigger budget, or a harder completion date. Yet in 2026 the largest public-works project on the U.S.-Mexico border in American history is underway largely beneath the national radar.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5e9d6285-7b10-407a-a9a0-f49794b965b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Where it began**
The wall wasn't born in 2016, but the promise was. Candidate Trump made it the spine of his campaign rallies, and historians may argue it helped propel him to victory that November ([U.S. News](https://www.usnews.com/news/politics/articles/2022-02-07/how-much-of-president-donald-trumps-border-wall-was-built)). First-term results were real but narrower than the rhetoric: roughly 458 miles of barrier built at a cost of about $15 billion -- though most of it replaced dilapidated fencing and vehicle barriers rather than walling virgin ground. Construction stopped on January 20, 2021, when President Biden issued a halt order on day one...

Fellow American,

This is the first and last email I'll ever send you.

You see, I'm a little unsure about opening up to you this way.

**But the deck is stacked against us, my back is against the wall, and your response to this message will decide everything.**

My name is Pat Harrigan. You don't know me, but I'm a Green Beret veteran from North Carolina. I graduated from West Point, and I served 18 months in combat.

After that, my wife and I started a firearm parts company from our double-wide trailer - and grew it to become a successful, job-creating business. And most important of all, I'm the dad of two beautiful girls.

**I'm honored to have won my race for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District in 2024, and I'm proud to work alongside President Trump to make our nation great again.**

With President Trump in the Oval Office and House and Senate Majorities in Congress, we're more equipped than ever to get our country back on track. The only thing we're missing is the resources to keep going.

| | Friend,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

**P.S.** There's one part of that phone call with Charlie I was going to leave out...

He wasn't just dreaming big -- he was issuing a warning.

When he told me we needed to move faster, he added: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. _**We don 't have time to wait.**_**" **

And he was right.

The Left has deeply embedded themselves in our schools -- rewriting history, poisoning young minds, and raising their next generation of radical foot soldiers.

We may be in 13% of our schools now...

_But in the other 87%? _

The Left has free rein. Zero resistance. No voice to challenge them.

And if we don't flood those schools with truth -- fast -- we'll have a generation that thinks loving America is "fascist," that faith is "hateful," and that freedom and free speech is "dangerous."

You know it. I know it. Charlie knew it.

He knew the fight for America's future would be won or lost in high school classrooms and on college campuses.

And that fight has never been more urgent than it is right now.

**Friend, if you 've ever wondered whether one small act could change the direction of our country -- _this is it._ **

You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do.

But you can send them the tools to do it.

These students are ready. They've raised their hands. They chose courage and decided to lead.

All they're waiting on... is us.

**Every $25 helps send an activism kit to a young patriot and gives them everything they need to win hearts and minds. **

You're gift reminds them they're not alone. It gives them the confidence to stand and fight back.

And you'll be saving our country -- one future freedom fighter at a time.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country... That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom. That 's what Club America is about... Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. But now, Friend, the question is... What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? Because here's the truth: These students aren't just signing up. They 're stepping up. They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous. But that isn't stopping them. They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever. They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, but brave. Not just loud, but principled. Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses. Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship. Charlie wanted a Club America chapter in every high school so no student would ever feel alone for loving God, defending their country, or believing in truth. And so the next generation wouldn't be handed over to the Left by default. Let's make Charlie's dream real -- 27,000 high schools. And a generation that doesn't apologize for loving this country. It's up to us to finish what he started. One chapter. One student. One school at a time. Let's move faster. Let's push further. Let's get this done -- for Charlie, and for the country we all love. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. There's one part of that phone call with Charlie I was going to leave out... He wasn't just dreaming big -- he was issuing a warning. When he told me we needed to move faster, he added: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. We don 't have time to wait." And he was right. The Left has deeply embedded themselves in our schools -- rewriting history, poisoning young minds, and raising their next generation of radical foot soldiers. We may be in 13% of our schools now... But in the other 87%? The Left has free rein. Zero resistance. No voice to challenge them. And if we don't flood those schools with truth -- fast -- we'll have a generation that thinks loving America is "fascist," that faith is "hateful," and that freedom and free speech is "dangerous." You know it. I know it. Charlie knew it. He knew the fight for America's future would be won or lost in high school classrooms and on college campuses. And that fight has never been more urgent than it is right now. Friend, if you 've ever wondered whether one small act could change the direction of our country -- this is it. You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do. But you can send them the tools to do it. These students are ready. They've raised their hands. They chose courage and decided to lead. All they're waiting on... is us. Every $25 helps send an activism kit to a young patriot and gives them everything they need to win hearts and minds. You're gift reminds them they're not alone. It gives them the confidence to stand and fight back. And you'll be saving our country -- one future freedom fighter at a time. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

**Tuesday, October 6, 2026 -**_****_
_**Yemen** : Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia activate Mecca defense pact, will deploy forces to Gulf kingdom against Houthis. Ansarallah strikes Saudi airport, Aramco refinery. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim capture of Mocha as coalition expands attacks on Ansarallah._
_**Iran** : U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent celebrates collective economic punishment of Iranians. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian calls U.S. negotiations "futile." U.S. President Donald Trump defends removal of U.S. bombers from UK base as seventh suspect arrested. Trump calls higher gas prices a "small price to pay" for war with Iran. Twelve sailors injured in attack on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz._
_**Palestine** : Israeli attacks kill three, wound several across Gaza. Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir joins demolition of Jerusalem apartment building as settlers torch Palestinian home, vehicles across the occupied West Bank. UK threatens to expel up to 27 Israeli diplomats over planned closure of East Jerusalem consulate. 111 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza in September._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli airstrikes, artillery and gunfire target southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire."_
_**U.S.** : Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee adds six deep-red districts to "Red to Blue" list, predicts House majority of up to 240 seats. Former President Barack Obama to campaign in Detroit with Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Soldiers wounded in March Iranian drone strike describe medical failures, red tape, AP reports. Supreme Court opens new term with Boulder climate case against Exxon, Suncor. Trump signs order allowing the use of untaxed off-road diesel on highways. Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. DOJ seeks to revoke citizenship of 40 naturalized Americans. Border agents raid Arizona protest camp, fell centuries-old cottonwood for Trump's border wall. Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agent sues federal government. Trump says New York Times, other outlets should be "arrested" over coverage of Ohio rally. Texas pediatricians face investigations from Attorney General and GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton over childhood vaccinations._
_**International:** Airstrikes, artillery hit northern Ethiopia as fighting continues. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, sworn in for a new term, insists Ethiopia must have Red Sea access. ISIS attack kills Iraqi federal policeman near Kirkuk, first since U.S. withdrawal. Russian bombs kill seven, injure over 60 in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia. Russia says Ukrainian drones struck Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing one. Ukraine blames Russian drones for sinking of grain ship in Romanian waters; two dead. Kuwait revokes citizenship of 415 more people, including billionaire Mahmoud Haider. Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of buying classified documents for foreign spy agency. Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court. Hundreds flee RSF assaults in Sudan's Blue Nile region. Cuba says it has "channels of communication" with the U.S. but no negotiations, and is preparing to defend itself. Mexico asks the U.S. for evidence of alleged cross-border gunfire at Coast Guard personnel. Parti Quebecois wins Quebec election. French teen loses hand in grenade blast as school protest clashes enter third week. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez calls snap election for Nov. 29._

# Yemen
* **Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia activate Mecca defense pact, will deploy forces to Gulf kingdom against Houthis:** Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia [agreed](https://substack.com/redirect/7e3df8e3-e159-4caf-9725-665ca62f3f80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday to activate "collective deterrence measures: under the Mecca Alliance for Defence after an emergency meeting of their defense and foreign ministers in Riyadh, the first time the pact, agreed to on August 7, has been invoked.
* Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said the alliance was responding to "the heinous attacks against the Kingdom and holy sites."
* A separate joint statement published by the Pakistani Foreign Ministry said the three would "provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment" to Saudi Arabia under approved arrangements.
* **Ansarallah strikes Saudi airport, Aramco refinery:** Ansarallah [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4d29c9bc-2891-459d-9642-aa7f63dac790?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it struck King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, disrupting air traffic, and an Aramco refinery in Rabigh, claiming to have set it on fire. It says it also hit Abha Airport, the Khamis Mushait airbase and other sites in Asir, Najran, and Jizan.
* The group warned all airlines to stop flying through Saudi airspace, calling it "a theater for our operations," with the exception of the airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
* It said the attacks were retaliation for 60 Saudi airstrikes and a missile on Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada, and Marib over 24 hours, which it said killed civilians. It says 1,576 Saudi strikes have hit Yemen since the escalation began.
* Three people were lightly injured and infrastructure damaged in attacks on King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport on Monday evening, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said.
* Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed Tuesday the group struck Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Asir province with a ballistic missile, disrupting air traffic, though Saudi authorities have not confirmed the attack.
* **Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim capture of Mocha as coalition expands attacks on Ansarallah:** Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces said Tuesday they had retaken the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha from Ansarallah following fighting south of the Bab al-Mandab strait, while the Saudi-led coalition announced a naval operation against Ansarallah in Hodeidah.
* The coalition separately said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa and a storage facility containing 20 ballistic missiles in Saada.
* Control of Mocha could provide government forces with a staging point for further operations along Yemen's Red Sea coast, though the situation on the ground remains fluid and competing territorial claims have emerged during recent fighting.
* Saudi-backed forces also claim to control Bab al-Mandab, an airport in Dhubab district and much of southwestern Taiz's Red Sea coastline, while Ansarallah officials say they repelled some advances and recaptured territory.

# Iran
* **Bessent celebrates collective economic punishment of Iranians:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [celebrated](https://substack.com/redirect/9653c291-58c7-4a49-98f4-b44182654e8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the collapse of Iran's economy, boasting that "Operation Economic Outcast is delivering results": the rial at record lows, and zero Iranian crude loaded onto tankers last month.
* "The Iranian regime allows its own people to suffer," Bessent claimed, as U.S. policies punish ordinary Iranian civilians.
* Nurses and teachers are quitting in large numbers because their salaries no longer cover the cost of living, the New York Times reported Monday.
* And the U.S. blockade and sanctions have cut imports of medicine and pharmaceutical raw materials, pushing prices up and leaving pharmacies short of drugs for serious illnesses, the FT reported. Some medicines have tripled in price.
* **Pezeshkian calls U.S. negotiations "futile": **Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that negotiations with the U.S. had become "futile," accusing Washington of repeatedly attacking Iran following talks and seeking to bring down the Islamic Republic.
* "Every time we come to the negotiating table, war is immediately imposed upon us," Pezeshkian said, according to IRNA, adding that the U.S. had attacked Iran three times following negotiations. "This demonstrates that they do not seek dialogue. On the contrary, their goal is to bring down the Islamic Republic of Iran."
* **Trump defends removal of U.S. bombers from UK base as seventh suspect arrested:** President Donald Trump on Monday defended the Pentagon's decision to remove B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in the UK following what he described as "some threats," after previously linking Iran to a security incident near the base.
* "Rather than tempting the enemy ... why should we leave them there? So, we moved them around a little bit. Not very far," Trump said, adding that Washington knows who made the threat and that "they've gotten themselves into big problems," without elaborating.
* UK counterterrorism police separately arrested a 22-year-old British national in Westminster on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in connection with activity near Fairford, bringing the number of arrests linked to the investigation over the past two weeks to seven.
* **Trump calls higher gas prices a "small price to pay" for war with Iran: **Trump said higher gasoline prices for U.S. consumers were a "small price to pay" for what he described as keeping the U.S. and the world safe, as the war with Iran continues to disrupt energy markets.
* Speaking at a Republican midterm campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, Trump said the price increase caused by the war was "just artificial" and "essentially almost over with," while repeating that the U.S. would not allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon.
* "They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles or San Diego. This is a very small price to pay," Trump said.
* He claimed gasoline prices would fall below $1.85 a gallon in "a very short period of time," potentially before or shortly after the November 3 midterm elections.
* **Twelve sailors injured in attack on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz:** Twelve sailors, including 11 Indian nationals, were injured in an attack on the Panama-flagged commercial vessel MT On Peace off Oman in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, India's Foreign Ministry said.
* The vessel was carrying 19 crew members, including 17 Indians. The injured sailors were evacuated with assistance from Omani authorities and are receiving treatment in Khasab.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed--one in a new Israeli attack and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and 35 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,245 killed, with 175,267 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,462 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,151, while 836 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli attacks kill three, wound several across Gaza:** An Israeli drone [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/83a383cc-966b-4020-bd74-e32964632c34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) near the municipal park in central Gaza City killed one Palestinian and wounded another on Tuesday, while several Palestinians were injured in a strike on Al-Wehda Street in the west of the city, WAFA reported. In Khan Younis, an Israeli attack killed two Palestinians, according to Al Jazeera
* Israeli forces also shot and wounded one person in the Karama neighborhood of northwest Gaza City and another near Bir 19, south of the Mawasi area of Khan Younis.
* **Ben-Gvir joins demolition of Jerusalem apartment building as settlers torch Palestinian home, vehicles across the occupied West Bank:**
* **East Jerusalem:** Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir [joined](https://substack.com/redirect/866bba9b-7f54-4419-ab67-5d16c668586e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israeli forces during the demolition of a five-story residential building in Al-Tur containing 10 apartments and housing about 70 Palestinians, mostly women and children, on Tuesday, according to WAFA.
* **Nablus:** Israeli bulldozers [razed](https://substack.com/redirect/affc91b1-f7cb-4a7d-8cb9-b559d42cf94c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) agricultural land and uprooted olive trees in Iraq Burin, while blocking several village roads with earth mounds. In Aqraba, settlers torched four Palestinian vehicles and spray-painted racist slogans.
* **Ramallah:** Settlers [set fire](https://substack.com/redirect/b57548b0-bab9-468d-ab91-563b707ba5ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a home housing a family of five in Burqa, causing extensive damage. The same homeowner, a U.S. citizen, had his vehicle damaged and dozens of his olive trees cut down by settlers about a month earlier.
* **Salfit:** Settlers attempted to set fire to a poultry structure and spray-painted racist slogans on a livestock farm in Farkha. Israeli forces separately raided Salfit city and [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/4825677f-e8f8-4c0a-bdc0-9a002f9eabeb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Nihad Al-Naoura, secretary of Fatah's Salfit branch.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/a701f79a-7228-4417-a601-f74ba301f279?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Bani Naim, declared the town a closed military zone, searched several homes and converted three into military posts.

Kuwait revokes citizenship of 415 more people, including billionaire Mahmoud Haider. Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of buying classified documents for foreign spy agency. Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court. Hundreds flee RSF assaults in Sudan's Blue Nile region. Cuba says it has "channels of communication" with the U.S. but no negotiations, and is preparing to defend itself. Mexico asks the U.S. for evidence of alleged cross-border gunfire at Coast Guard personnel. Parti Quebecois wins Quebec election. French teen loses hand in grenade blast as school protest clashes enter third week. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez calls snap election for Nov. 29. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia activate Mecca defense pact, will deploy forces to Gulf kingdom against Houthis: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Monday to activate "collective deterrence measures: under the Mecca Alliance for Defence after an emergency meeting of their defense and foreign ministers in Riyadh, the first time the pact, agreed to on August 7, has been invoked. Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said the alliance was responding to "the heinous attacks against the Kingdom and holy sites." A separate joint statement published by the Pakistani Foreign Ministry said the three would "provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment" to Saudi Arabia under approved arrangements. Ansarallah strikes Saudi airport, Aramco refinery: Ansarallah it struck King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, disrupting air traffic, and an Aramco refinery in Rabigh, claiming to have set it on fire. It says it also hit Abha Airport, the Khamis Mushait airbase and other sites in Asir, Najran, and Jizan. The group warned all airlines to stop flying through Saudi airspace, calling it "a theater for our operations," with the exception of the airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. It said the attacks were retaliation for 60 Saudi airstrikes and a missile on Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada, and Marib over 24 hours, which it said killed civilians. It says 1,576 Saudi strikes have hit Yemen since the escalation began. Three people were lightly injured and infrastructure damaged in attacks on King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport on Monday evening, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed Tuesday the group struck Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Asir province with a ballistic missile, disrupting air traffic, though Saudi authorities have not confirmed the attack. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim capture of Mocha as coalition expands attacks on Ansarallah: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces said Tuesday they had retaken the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha from Ansarallah following fighting south of the Bab al-Mandab strait, while the Saudi-led coalition announced a naval operation against Ansarallah in Hodeidah. The coalition separately said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa and a storage facility containing 20 ballistic missiles in Saada. Control of Mocha could provide government forces with a staging point for further operations along Yemen's Red Sea coast, though the situation on the ground remains fluid and competing territorial claims have emerged during recent fighting. Saudi-backed forces also claim to control Bab al-Mandab, an airport in Dhubab district and much of southwestern Taiz's Red Sea coastline, while Ansarallah officials say they repelled some advances and recaptured territory. Iran Bessent celebrates collective economic punishment of Iranians: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent the collapse of Iran's economy, boasting that "Operation Economic Outcast is delivering results": the rial at record lows, and zero Iranian crude loaded onto tankers last month. "The Iranian regime allows its own people to suffer," Bessent claimed, as U.S. policies punish ordinary Iranian civilians. Nurses and teachers are quitting in large numbers because their salaries no longer cover the cost of living, the New York Times reported Monday. And the U.S. blockade and sanctions have cut imports of medicine and pharmaceutical raw materials, pushing prices up and leaving pharmacies short of drugs for serious illnesses, the FT reported. Some medicines have tripled in price. Pezeshkian calls U.S. negotiations "futile": Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that negotiations with the U.S. had become "futile," accusing Washington of repeatedly attacking Iran following talks and seeking to bring down the Islamic Republic. "Every time we come to the negotiating table, war is immediately imposed upon us," Pezeshkian said, according to IRNA, adding that the U.S. had attacked Iran three times following negotiations. "This demonstrates that they do not seek dialogue. On the contrary, their goal is to bring down the Islamic Republic of Iran." Trump defends removal of U.S. bombers from UK base as seventh suspect arrested: President Donald Trump on Monday defended the Pentagon's decision to remove B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in the UK following what he described as "some threats," after previously linking Iran to a security incident near the base. "Rather than tempting the enemy ... why should we leave them there? So, we moved them around a little bit. Not very far," Trump said, adding that Washington knows who made the threat and that "they've gotten themselves into big problems," without elaborating. UK counterterrorism police separately arrested a 22-year-old British national in Westminster on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in connection with activity near Fairford, bringing the number of arrests linked to the investigation over the past two weeks to seven. Trump calls higher gas prices a "small price to pay" for war with Iran: Trump said higher gasoline prices for U.S. consumers were a "small price to pay" for what he described as keeping the U.S. and the world safe, as the war with Iran continues to disrupt energy markets. Speaking at a Republican midterm campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, Trump said the price increase caused by the war was "just artificial" and "essentially almost over with," while repeating that the U.S. would not allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon. "They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles or San Diego. This is a very small price to pay," Trump said. He claimed gasoline prices would fall below $1.85 a gallon in "a very short period of time," potentially before or shortly after the November 3 midterm elections. Twelve sailors injured in attack on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz: Twelve sailors, including 11 Indian nationals, were injured in an attack on the Panama-flagged commercial vessel MT On Peace off Oman in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, India's Foreign Ministry said. The vessel was carrying 19 crew members, including 17 Indians. The injured sailors were evacuated with assistance from Omani authorities and are receiving treatment in Khasab. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed--one in a new Israeli attack and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and 35 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,245 killed, with 175,267 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,462 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,151, while 836 bodies have been recovered. Israeli attacks kill three, wound several across Gaza: An Israeli drone near the municipal park in central Gaza City killed one Palestinian and wounded another on Tuesday, while several Palestinians were injured in a strike on Al-Wehda Street in the west of the city, WAFA reported. In Khan Younis, an Israeli attack killed two Palestinians, according to Al Jazeera Israeli forces also shot and wounded one person in the Karama neighborhood of northwest Gaza City and another near Bir 19, south of the Mawasi area of Khan Younis. Ben-Gvir joins demolition of Jerusalem apartment building as settlers torch Palestinian home, vehicles across the occupied West Bank: East Jerusalem: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir Israeli forces during the demolition of a five-story residential building in Al-Tur containing 10 apartments and housing about 70 Palestinians, mostly women and children, on Tuesday, according to WAFA. Nablus: Israeli bulldozers agricultural land and uprooted olive trees in Iraq Burin, while blocking several village roads with earth mounds. In Aqraba, settlers torched four Palestinian vehicles and spray-painted racist slogans. Ramallah: Settlers to a home housing a family of five in Burqa, causing extensive damage. The same homeowner, a U.S. citizen, had his vehicle damaged and dozens of his olive trees cut down by settlers about a month earlier. Salfit: Settlers attempted to set fire to a poultry structure and spray-painted racist slogans on a livestock farm in Farkha. Israeli forces separately raided Salfit city and Nihad Al-Naoura, secretary of Fatah's Salfit branch. Hebron: Israeli forces Bani Naim, declared the town a closed military zone, searched several homes and converted three into military posts. UK threatens to expel up to 27 Israeli diplomats over planned closure of East Jerusalem consulate: The UK to expel one Israeli diplomat for every British diplomat forced out of Israel over Israel's plan to close the UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem on Thursday, which could mean as many as 27 expulsions, Ynet reported. The Foreign Office declined to comment on "speculation" rather than denying the report. Israel threatened to close the consulate this week, as part of its response to the UK's ban on trade in goods from illegal West Bank settlements and sanctions on British firms aiding settlement construction. The British Foreign Office was reportedly advised by former UK attorney general Dominic Grieve that such an action would be illegal, given that the United Nations and most of its members recognize East Jerusalem as Palestinian territory. 111 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza in September: Israeli forces 111 Palestinians in Gaza in September, including 23 children, ten women and four elderly people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry's monthly report. Israel has killed Palestinians in Gaza every month since the ceasefire began. The deadliest month was July, with 152 killed. Lebanon Israeli airstrikes, artillery and gunfire target southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire": Israeli warplanes strikes on Wadi Al-Salouqi and an area between Bra'shit and Aitaroun in the Bint Jbeil district overnight, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery the outskirts of Hadatha and Bra'shit, while Israeli forces opened machine-gun fire toward Bayt Al-Sayyad and the outskirts of Mansouri. U.S. News DCCC adds six deep-red districts to "Red to Blue" list, predicts House majority of up to 240 seats: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee six candidates to its "Red to Blue" list Monday, in districts Trump won by an average of 16 points or more in 2024, signalling that the Democratic Party will allocate extra resources, and perhaps fundraising dollars, to these races. The six include: Arkansas's 2nd, where Democrat Chris Jones faces incumbent Rep. French Hill ; Colorado's 3rd, where Democrat Dwayne Romero faces incumbent Rep. Jeff Hurd ; Florida's 27th, where Eliott Rodriguez faces incumbent Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar ; New York's 21st, where Democrat Blake Gendebien faces Republican Anthony Constantino ; Nevada's 2nd, where Democrat Teresa Benitez-Thompson faces Republican David Flippo ; and Tennessee's 9th, where DemocratJustin J. Pearson faces Republican Brent Taylor. DCCC political director Brooke Butler told Politico that "anywhere between 218 and 240 feels very viable" for Democrats' potential House majority and that more seats could be added, "if gas keeps going and diesel kicks back up." Obama to campaign in Detroit with El-Sayed, Benson on Oct. 24: Former President Barack Obama will in Detroit on Saturday, Oct. 24, with Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed , gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and other candidates, the Michigan Democratic Party announced Monday. El-Sayed faces Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in the race to succeed retiring Sen. Gary Peters , while Benson, the secretary of state, faces Republican Rep. John James in the open governor's race. Obama has made few public stops on the trail this year but previously campaigned in Texas with Senate nominee James Talarico and gubernatorial nominee Gina Hinojosa and appeared in a campaign ad with Iowa Senate nominee Josh Turek. He is also set to headline a Washington-area fundraiser Wednesday for the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Soldiers wounded in March Iranian drone strike describe medical failures, red tape, AP reports: Nine U.S. service members in the March 1 Iranian drone strike at Port Shuaiba, Kuwait, which killed six troops on the second day of the Iran war, spoke on the record to the Associated Press about what they describe as a medical system that left them fighting for treatment on their own. Lt. Col. Arturo Linc on, who suffered shrapnel wounds to his jaw, neck, and spine, including a severed vertebral artery, was sent to barracks and told to seek outpatient appointments after Landstuhl Regional Medical Center in Germany did not admit him. Chief Warrant Officer 4 Rodney Bearman said he and others injured in the attacks were not properly registered as "wounded in combat" due to a coding error. Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom said he waited over four months for MRI results and has "had to build my own case for everything." Lincon, who still has shrapnel near his spinal cord and struggles with dizziness, told the AP that, following the attacks, in which his passport was destroyed, he was issued a temporary substitute and asked to prove his citizenship in the process (he was born in Texas to Mexican parents and graduated from West Point). He was also denied a Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance injury claim. Supreme Court opens new term with Boulder climate case against Exxon, Suncor: The Supreme Court's new term Monday with arguments in Boulder's lawsuit accusing Exxon Mobil and Suncor Energy of deceiving the public about the harms of fossil fuels. Boulder says it is seeking to recover past and future costs of repairs, emergency services and property damage, not to regulate emissions. The companies argue that only the federal government has the power to address something as large as climate change. The Trump administration has sided with them in the case. Justice Samuel Alito stepped aside a week before argument, after calls for recusal over his stock in Phillips 66 and ConocoPhillips. A 4-4 tie would leave the Colorado Supreme Court's ruling allowing the suit to proceed in place. Trump signs order allowing the use of untaxed off-road diesel on highways: President Donald Trump an executive order on Monday temporarily allowing red-dyed diesel, normally reserved for farm and industrial vehicles, to be used on highways while deferring the 24.4-cent-per-gallon federal excise tax for the rest of the year, according to a fact sheet released by the White House. Diesel prices have surged from $3.76 a gallon before the war in Iran to a record $6.53 on September 22, according to AAA. The change could potentially save truckers roughly $150 per fill-up, according to CNN, though experts noted it does nothing to improve the principal cause of rising fuel prices, a global shortage of working refineries. Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan: Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell Monday on X that War Secretary Pete Hegseth "recommended" and President Trump "approved" death by firing squad for Nidal Malik Hasan , the convicted terrorist who killed 13 people and wounded 32 in the 2009 Fort Hood attack. Parnell said the Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. At least 144 civilian prisoners have been executed by shooting since 1608, according to the AP, the most recent being South Carolina's Brad Sigmon last year, who chose the method over the electric chair and lethal injection. DOJ seeks to revoke citizenship of 40 naturalized Americans in largest denaturalization push in recent history: The Justice Department is to revoke the citizenship of 40 foreign-born Americans it accuses of lying about or omitting criminal histories on their naturalization applications, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced in a press release Monday. The government accuses the applicants of having committed crimes including espionage, transporting child pornography, sexual misconduct against a minor, and voluntary manslaughter. The cases far exceed the average of 15 a year under previous administrations. DOJ announced that it would target as many as 300 people for possible denaturalization in April. Border agents raid Arizona protest camp, fell centuries-old cottonwood for Trump 's border wall: More than 50 Customs and Border Protection agents an activist camp in Lochiel, Arizona, on Monday, ending a 70-day protest of a potential tree demolition. Following the raid, an excavator knocked down the tree, a 150-to-250-year-old cottonwood, known as the "grandmother tree," that stood in the path of President Donald Trump's $46.5 billion border wall expansion. Activists told the Washington Post that agents dragged, kicked, and knelt on protesters during a sunrise prayer ceremony, with about 10 arrested and another 10 cited. Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agent sues federal government: Marimar Martinez , a Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agentCharles Exum , the federal government Monday for false arrest and imprisonment, malicious prosecution, emotional distress, and negligence, with her attorneys saying an independent crime scene analysis shows the agent shot her as she turned her car away from him. Shortly after the shooting, DHS called Martinez a "domestic terrorist" and charged her, but the charges were later dropped. Exum was later placed on "administrative leave," the department noted, "consistent with policy." Martinez said she was prepared to let the matter go after charges against her were dropped, until federal agents killed two people in Minneapolis. "What's happening is not normal," she added. Trump says New York Times, other outlets should be "arrested" over coverage of Ohio rally: President Trump on Truth Social Monday that the New York Times and "many other Artificial Media Outlets, should be arrested for their dishonesty and disservice to our Country," after Times correspondent Katie Rogers reported that "several areas of an upper deck were empty" by the end of his Saturday rally at Butler High School in Vandalia, Ohio. Trump disputed the paper's claims about attendance, saying that the arena was "totally MAXED OUT" and claiming thousands were turned away at the doors. Texas pediatricians face Paxton investigations over childhood vaccinations: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , the Republican U.S. Senate nominee, a statewide investigation accusing doctors, drug companies and insurers of conspiring to push parents into vaccinating children, with a New York Times report on Monday highlighting the case of " Dr. Rachel," a central Texas pediatrician of 20 years who says responding to that investigation has cost her nearly $15,000 in legal fees and prompted her to reconsider her career. A December letter from the AG's office demanded 10 years of vaccine purchase records and her practice's vaccine policy, and said citing the CDC schedule would not suffice. In August, Paxton opened a separate probe of the American Academy of Pediatrics for "deceptively promoting childhood vaccines for financial gain." Pediatricians reject the profit motive as ludicrous, noting they pay for vaccines upfront and that nearly half of children's vaccines are covered by the federal Vaccines for Children program. Texas kindergarten measles and polio vaccine coverage has fallen to about 93 percent from nearly 97 percent in 2019. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Airstrikes, artillery hit northern Ethiopia as fighting continues after fall of Mekelle: Airstrikes at least 17 people overnight into Monday in Tigray, nine in Adwa, and eight in Sheraro, according to a humanitarian bulletin cited by Reuters, which could not confirm the reports or who launched the strikes. Government forces and fighters loyal to the Tigray People's Liberation Front also exchanged heavy artillery fire near the Tekeze River close to Mai Tsebri on Monday. In Mekelle, which Tigrayan forces left without a fight, residents said that shops were reopening and that phone and internet access was returning after a week-long disruption. Abiy, sworn in for a new term, insists Ethiopia must have Red Sea access: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Parliament Monday, as he was sworn in for another five-year term, that Ethiopia will work to secure a Red Sea port, saying "based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea" and calling access critical to the country's "civilization." His remarks came a day after Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan, and Somalia met in New Alamein and declared that governance of the Red Sea is the "exclusive responsibility" of the region's coastal states. Eritrea has accused Ethiopia of seeking to reassert control over its coast, which it lost when Eritrea gained its independence from Ethiopia in 1993. ISIS attack kills Iraqi federal policeman near Kirkuk, first since U.S. withdrawal: At least one Iraqi federal policeman was and four wounded Monday when Islamic State militants attacked a federal police regiment near Hawija, about 70 km southwest of Kirkuk, using semi-automatic machine guns and sniper fire, two security sources told Reuters. No group has claimed responsibility, but security and army sources said ISIS militants, who retain sleeper cells in the area, were involved. It is the first reported ISIS assault on Iraqi security forces since the U.S. completed its military withdrawal from Iraq on Sept. 30. Russian bombs kill seven, injure over 60 in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia: Three Russian bombs different areas of the northeastern Ukrainian city Kharkiv on Monday, killing six people and injuring 59, according to regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. Three of those injured in Monday's attacks on Kharkiv were children. Elsewhere on Monday, a Russian drone hit an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, injuring three people who were trapped on the ninth floor, according to that region's governor. Russian airstrikes also killed one person in Sloviansk in the Donetsk region. Russia says Ukrainian drones struck Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing one: Ukrainian drones a laboratory building and a radioactive waste processing facility at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant overnight on Monday, killing a driver delivering food to plant workers, according to Alexei Likhachev, head of Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom, who said there was no threat to nuclear safety. Ukraine blames Russian drones for sinking of grain ship in Romanian waters; two dead: Romania's Interior Ministry two people were killed and 11 rescued after a grain ship caught fire and sank Monday in Romania's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea; the ministry did not identify the cause of the fire. Azerbaijani and Indian nationals were reportedly aboard. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the fire, condemning in a Monday post on X the "horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye." Kuwait revokes citizenship of 415 more people, including billionaire Mahmoud Haider: Kuwait six decrees published in its official gazette stripping 415 people of citizenship, including billionaire businessman Mahmoud Haider, along with dependents who obtained nationality through those whose citizenship was revoked. The Gulf state announced a citizenship review campaign in 2024, targeting fraudulent claims, including those involving individuals reporting dual nationality or those who acquired it through marriage. It has expanded this year to politicians, footballers, and musicians, including 1982 World Cup goalkeeper Ahmed al-Tarabulsi and singer Abdulmohsen Al Muhanna. Rights groups estimate at least 50,000 people have lost citizenship since 2024. Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of buying classified documents for foreign spy agency: Former Federal Intelligence Service chief August Hanning was on Tuesday on suspicion of paying a former office manager at the agency for roughly 2,000 documents, including classified material and senior intelligence briefings prepared for the chancellery, and using them to draft an analysis for an officer of an unnamed foreign intelligence service, according to German federal prosecutors. Prosecutors allege the arrangement began in 2010, five years after Hanning left the agency, and that he also shared political information with a representative of a second foreign intelligence service. The office manager, identified only as Manfred D., was also arrested. The case does not involve Russia, according to the German newspaper Suddeutsche Zeitung. Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court: Police tear gas and water cannons Monday evening against several hundred protesters, including veterans and supporters of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army, outside Parliament in Pristina after lawmakers adjourned without passing amendments limiting the powers of the controversial Kosovo Specialist Chambers court. Twelve people were injured, including 11 civilians, according to a Pristina hospital emergency director. The amendments, which passed a first reading earlier Monday, would cap the court's sentences at 15 years, allow these to be served in Kosovo and permit appeals to Kosovo's Supreme Court. They were forwarded by the opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) and halted by Prime Minister Albin Kurti's governing Vetevendosje party. The court remains controversial in Kosovo, where the KLA, which the court was created to prosecute, is held in high esteem by many in the country's Albanian population after its fight against the Serbian-dominated Yugoslav government during Kosovo's 1998-1999 war. Hundreds flee RSF assaults in Sudan 's Blue Nile region: Hundreds of residents have the localities of Jabal Al-Nimr and Minza in Sudan's southeastern Blue Nile region after recent Rapid Support Forces attacks, the region's Humanitarian Aid Commission said on Monday. Most are heading toward the town of Al-Azaza and a settlement known as Village 6, raising concerns over civilian protection and shortages of essential supplies. Cuba says it has "channels of communication" with the U.S. but no negotiations, and is preparing to defend itself: Cuba's charge d'affaires in Washington, Lianys Torres Rivera, Reuters on Monday that Havana and Washington maintain "channels of communication"--including meetings, phone calls, and WhatsApp messages--but are not in formal negotiations and have made no progress toward restarting official talks. Rivera's remarks contradict President Donald Trump's claim last month at the UN that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was "deep into negotiations" with Havana. Torres Rivera said Cuba remains open to "respectful" dialogue with the U.S. but is "not naive" about Trump's threats and is expanding its defense preparations, saying "we are increasing our capabilities now more than ever before." She also noted that Cuba's "red line" remains changes to its political system. Mexico asks U.S. for evidence of alleged cross-border gunfire at Coast Guard personnel: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Monday her government has requested evidence from U.S. authorities about allegations that shots were fired from the Mexican side of the border at U.S. personnel, saying "we asked for all the evidence because we have no evidence" and that no National Guard, Army, or Navy personnel detected shots fired from Mexican territory toward the U.S. The comments came a day after U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said on X that "shots were fired at U.S. Coast Guard personnel" in an area where Tamaulipas meets Texas. The incident follows Mexico's announcement of "Operation Mirror" on Sunday evening, a joint border security effort deploying 500 troops, helicopters, drones and anti-drone equipment along the frontier. Despite deepening security collaboration, Sheinbaum has repeatedly denied that her government would allow a U.S. military intervention on Mexican soil. Parti Qu ebecois wins Quebec election, complicating Carney's unity push against Trump: The separatist party Parti Quebecois, by Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, won Quebec's election Monday, according to early projections from public broadcaster Radio-Canada, though it remains too early to say whether the party secured a majority in the province's legislature. The result, widely expected before the vote, will jettison the center-right Coalition Avenir Quebec government, which has been in office since 2018. St-Pierre Plamondon has promised a referendum on leaving Canada, but only once Trump is out of the White House. Previous independence referendums failed in 1980 and 1995, and current polling puts support for a separation at around 30 percent. St-Pierre Plamondon pledged to work with Carney when it suits the province's interests; his party notably diverges from Ottawa in its calls to reduce immigration, cut Quebec's ties to the British monarchy, and efforts to block a proposed Quebec-Ontario high-speed rail line. French teen loses hand in grenade blast as school protest clashes enter third week: A 15-year-old boy lost a hand Monday near a high school in Lens after an explosion that unverified police reports said involved a stun grenade. He is hospitalized in Lille, and his life is not in danger, according to Pas-de-Calais's regional prefect. Police internal affairs is now handling six investigations into serious injuries during the protests; the country's Education Minister, Edouard Geffray, said Monday that 190 students have been injured since the unrest began. His ministry also noted that 589 schools were disrupted Monday, down from 735 Friday, and about 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested since Sept. 28. Amnesty International France criticized the government's use of "disproportionate force" against minors during the weeks-long protests. Spain 's Sanchez calls snap election for Nov. 29 after Parliament rejects housing relief measures: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez in a televised address on Monday that Spain will hold a general election on Nov. 29, after Parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government. The announcement follows weeks of nationwide housing protests, including a Saturday demonstration in Madrid that the government said drew more than 70,000 people, motivated in part by the televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid. Average rents in Spain have nearly doubled over the past decade, according to data from the Spanish real estate firm Idealista. The conservative People's Party, led by Alberto Nuñez Feijoo and backed by the far-right Vox party, appears poised to win in November, according to early polling. If it does, it would become the first far-right party to control the country's central government since the death of fascist dictator Francisco Franco in 1975. Midterms are a crucial opportunity for all of us to look inwards and think about how our vote can help future generations.
While my opponent has doubled down on the war in Iran, on tariffs and policies that take money out of the pockets of North Carolinians, I'm focused on making life easier for hardworking people that deserve a change.
As I told Lawrence on MS NOW, Washington could use a little North Carolina common sense. We have to make sure our neighbors are voting, our co-workers are voting and our family members are voting, because this is a critical time in the history of our country. If you're ready to flip the Senate and drain the swamp in Washington, I hope you'll consider [chipping in a few dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [signing up to volunteer. ](https://substack.com/redirect/9a67ad99-5117-48d2-9de9-bb295f6c163d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Every effort counts.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/9a67ad99-5117-48d2-9de9-bb295f6c163d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
P.S. You can watch the full interview here and read the transcript below.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1d86225b-b0a9-4ef9-b717-769dddde1068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
**Gov. Cooper:** _I appreciate your optimism, and I 'm hopeful that we can win this race and that we can take back the Senate and take back the House. We need a course correction for our country. But we know that there is a lot of big money out there, and there is a culture of DC insiders that are fueled by big money and my opponent, Michael Whatley, has been one of them for years. A lobbyist for utility companies and big oil companies._
_And the thing about it is, he has continued to do and say whatever Donald Trump has told him to do and say, regardless of whether it 's good for the people of North Carolina. So he has doubled down on the tariffs. He has doubled down on the war in Iran. He has cheered on all of these policies. And the thing about it is, he owns the stock. He owns the individual stocks of all of these companies that he's cheering for. When he cheers on the war in Iran, oil stocks go up, money goes out of the pockets of people of North Carolina and into his. When utility companies raise their rates, he owns their stock, money goes out of the pockets of the people of North Carolina and into his. And the thing about it is that they are fueling these campaigns.**People can go to[roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/753ff5c0-b987-44f5-bfec-31b88569fb66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and help us out.**_
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_You worry about negative ads and deceptive ads that continue to lie over and over and over again. You worry about people believing it. But I 'm going to continue to hope that we can get our message out and to make sure that we are setting the record straight because people know how they feel, and they know this war in Iran is driving up gas prices. They know that these tariffs are causing them to pay more at the grocery store and whenever they buy something. And connecting those dots is really important for us right now._
**Lawrence O 'Donnell:** _One thing about both you and Sherrod Brown is that your states know you. They know you both. They 've elected you statewide before: Sherrod Brown in Ohio, you in North Carolina. Do you think that helps you survive just this carpet bombing of negative ads against you?_
**Gov. Cooper:** _That 's a really good point, Lawrence. When I left the Governor's office, I thought I might do something else. But then, when this administration took root and I saw things happening almost every single day that reached a new level of chaos, any one of which we could talk about for hours, I knew that I needed to step up and run for this Senate seat, because I knew how much money was going to come down._
_And look, I 'm going to be first in line to try and overturn Citizens United. We have to do that. But I knew that this was going to happen. I also knew that the people of North Carolina. I developed some trust with them, and I was hoping that it would take them a long time to believe negative ads that were not true, and hopefully many of them would never believe it. And I thought that that would give me an advantage, that I had the best chance to win. We haven't elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in almost two decades, and we've only elected two Democrats in almost 40 years. So that's one of the reasons why I stepped up because I knew that a lot of people were being left behind._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5ac8783a-4c86-403f-8b3d-225c36d14198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_I saw this Washington controlled by DC insiders. I believed that Washington could use a little North Carolina common sense. I knew how to work across the aisle and get things done. Expanded Medicaid in North Carolina, 640,000 new, better-paying jobs. And I can take those receipts to Washington, and I believe I can get things done. But we 've got to get through this campaign, and we cannot stop. We all have to, across this country. We can't sit back and smile about polling leads or dissatisfaction with the president. We have to run through the tape._
_We have to make sure our neighbors are voting, our co-workers are voting, our family members are voting, because this is a critical time in the history of our country. And these midterms are a time when all of us can look inside ourselves and think this is something that I can do for future generations to make sure we make the change that we know we have to make right now._

The scent of damp earth and the heat of a turning pile signal a quiet revolution. In the compost, decay is not an end, but a profound transformation.
Just as a child mimics a parent to build soul, we must learn to mimic nature's unbreakable logic. Nature never discards; it integrates. This is the grit of the Kitchen Table--the refusal to let anything go to waste, the ability to take the broken and turn it into sustenance. To master this mimicry is to reclaim our agency, transforming the debris of our existence into the fortification of our ground.
Decomposition is the biological conversion of organic matter into nutrient-dense soil.

Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**

Peter,

We're officially **less than one month away** from Election Day.

That means we're officially entering the final stretch — and simply can't afford to take even a single day between now and November 3rd for granted.

Look, Wesley ran for Congress because he believes St. Louis deserves a representative who will show up, listen, and fight for the people who call this community home. And since taking office, that's exactly what he's been focused on doing.

He's worked to bring federal investments home to St. Louis, expand opportunities for workers, support our HBCUs, and make sure our community has a voice in Washington. **But Wesley also knows that the work ahead is bigger than any one district.** Right now, Republicans hold the House majority by just a handful of seats.

I’ve been crisscrossing Iowa nonstop, and with the latest polls neck and neck with my radical Liberal opponent, Josh Turek, I don’t see things slowing down anytime soon. | My team and I have been out on the campaign trail talking to Iowans and grassroots patriots just like you every day. I’ve gone from meeting with local leaders from Fort Dodge to knocking doors in Sioux City and enjoying the Plymouth County Fair in Le Mars recently. I promise to never be outworked, but by the looks of what’s next, we’re about to be outraised and outspent at every turn for the final stretch of this make-or-break election. Every penny will be put to good use to fully fuel my campaign to victory. Protecting Iowa is the ONLY way we can make sure we protect the Senate Majority and save our GOP agenda. Thank you for hearing me out, and I promise to keep you up to date on the latest here in Iowa. Friends, it’s James Carville here.
This ain’t my first rodeo. I’ve been around politics a long time, so TRUST me: I know which races are THE races to pay attention to and invest in.
Folks, I’m telling you that North Carolina will determine control of the Senate this November. Roy Cooper’s Senate race in the Tar Heel State is NECK AND NECK, and the only way he can swing it in his direction is with overwhelming grassroots support from folks like YOU.
[**So please: Will you chip in $10 or whatever you can spare right now between Cooper and GIFFORDS PAC?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-cooper26.zFyL5o&refcode=em261006-1-b&t=2&akid=11900%2E3935704%2EYk85uE)
What’s happening in our country right now is batsh*t crazy. Truly.
Billionaires and special interests making millions on the backs of working families. Folks struggling to put food on the table and afford basic needs. Republicans taking away health care from everyday people to give more money and access to the richest folks in America.
**We’ve got to fix what’s broken in Washington DC, and electing Roy in North Carolina is CRITICAL to making that happen.**
Roy has served the people of North Carolina for decades, and he’s ready to keep up this work in the Senate.
**But GOP super PACs are pouring over $100 MILLION – yes, that’s 1-0-0 – into this race to defeat Roy and turn voters against him, and he needs our urgent support to fight back.**
[**Democrats have NO chance at taking back the Senate without winning in North Carolina, so your donation today could not be more important. Will you chip in $10 or more to help GIFFORDS PAC and Roy flip NC?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-cooper26.zFyL5o&refcode=em261006-1-b&t=3&akid=11900%2E3935704%2EYk85uE)

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/_WWv3gdC9Nm?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

Friend,

Horrible Hobbs has a four-point lead over conservative Andy Biggs in Arizona.

We can’t trust every poll, but here’s how we like to operate. Pray as though it all depends on God and act as though it all depends on us.

To put it simply, we cannot lose Arizona to Democrats in 2026.

Here’s why:

If we lose Arizona in 2026, we don't just lose one election. We may lose the next decade.

**Arizona controls 11 electoral votes. Soon, it'll be 12. Without Arizona, roughly 70% of the statistical paths to the White House disappear. **

>>> Whoever is the governor of Arizona will oversee the 2028 election. We need to win to secure the election.

>>> Arizona is the most consequential state in the presidential election. Lose it here, and 2028 gets a lot harder to win.

>>> Whoever wins the White House in 2028 runs the census. Whoever runs the census draws the lines for 2032.

That's a decade of ground we don't get back.

Here’s how we win Arizona:

We win by deploying real people, knocking on doors, building real relationships with real voters.

It’s having ballot chasers in the field every single day until Election Day.

We've done it before. Our ballot chasers helped beat a Kamala-backed city councilwoman here in Arizona. They delivered a win in the Salt River Project race against a wall of environmental spending.

And of course, it’s how we delivered Arizona for Trump in 2028!

This works. We've proven it works.

Now we need to fund it at scale.

**Turning Point PAC is trying to raise $94,000 this week to put ballot chasers in the field across Arizona.**

Every dollar we raise goes straight to funding that operation: training, deploying, and sustaining the people who chase the vote.

I buy vinyl records from Europe and Australia. For years the math worked: a €22 pressing shipped from Hamburg still beat the same record at a Nashville shop, even after Tennessee's 9.75% sales tax. Foreign supply disciplined domestic prices and kept rare catalog titles reachable.
That math is now broken -- not because records got tariffed, but because a customs rule that made small parcels frictionless is gone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2162f81-ef17-476c-8f10-81ed0ff2f455?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**What de minimis was**
Section 321 of the 1930 Tariff Act let goods worth $800 or less enter the U.S. duty-free with almost no paperwork. The threshold was raised to $800 in 2016, and by fiscal 2024 roughly 1.4 billion packages a year came in through it. It's the reason a one-woman Etsy shop in Lisbon or a used-record seller in Melbourne could ship to an American buyer as easily as mailing an envelope. That was the cheap-foreign-alternative engine...

** Let's Finish what Caroline Kane started and Make TX-07 Red Again
